opener_episode.title: 1382: Emad Mostaque | Surviving the Coming AI Jobs Apocalypse
opener_episode.why: Recent flagship guest interview; Mostaque's 'what is left of value when AI can make anything' theme sets up Avery's contrarian take that scarcity, provenance and human story are why collectors still pay six figures for physical art. Alternative opener: Jamison Firestone (1389) if pitching the opaque-markets/trust angle.

angles.headline: Manufacturing an art star: how hype, scarcity and story turned a street artist into a global brand
angles.pitch: Avery breaks down the psychology he used to take Alec Monopoly from street walls to sold-out shows from New York to Morocco and major brand partnerships, and what it reveals about how status and desire are created.
angles.builds_on: Show's recurring status/persuasion themes (e.g., Will Storr 'status game' episode) and the Emad Mostaque episode on value in an AI economy

angles.headline: Inside the room when celebrities buy art: fame, money and outlandish requests
angles.pitch: The dealer who placed a $100K+ Hap Tivey work with Kris Jenner at Art Basel Miami Beach 2024 explains how the very rich actually decide what to buy, and where the art market's opacity creates risk for buyers.
angles.builds_on: Jamison Firestone (1389) on opaque systems and the show's long-running scams/fraud category (incl. art forger Ken Perenyi, Ep. 282)

angles.headline: Why physical art survives the digital gold rush
angles.pitch: Having launched one of the first online-only blue-chip galleries in 2015 and sold an NFT of Michael Cohen's prison badge via ArtGrails (Vanity Fair, 2021), Avery explains what actually holds value when anything can be copied or generated.
angles.builds_on: Emad Mostaque (1382) and Rob Reid (1390) on exponential tech

booking.route: Contact page (jordanharbinger.com/contact) invites guest suggestions; Jordan says he reads his inbox and is open to publicist pitches. friday@jordanharbinger.com is published for Feedback Friday questions/guest suggestions (not a booking desk). Jen Harbinger is listed on the team page as manager overseeing the podcast/business. Warm-intro option: David Packouz has been a JHS guest ('The Real-Life War Dogs Gun Runner') and has also been a guest on Avery's podcast.
booking.contact: https://www.jordanharbinger.com/contact/ ; friday@jordanharbinger.com (listener/feedback inbox) ; team: Jen Harbinger (manager, per team page)

format: Three episodes a week: long-form guest interviews (typically ~1-2h, unverified), plus Feedback Friday and Skeptical Sunday. Remote guests have recorded via SquadCast/Skype with local audio (per earlier research; unverified for 2026). Jordan does 10-20h prep per guest and does not send questions in advance. Typical guests: authors, journalists, intelligence/crime insiders, scientists; recent run heavy on geopolitics, Russia, AI and biosecurity. Studio city: Los Angeles area per earlier research (unverified). Very large audience (show claims millions of monthly downloads).
red_flags: No dedicated booking email published; contact form/inbox only
Strong preference for guests with a book or concrete project; publicist-driven inflow
Will reject promotional pitches: pitch insight/story, not ArtLife
Guests are not paid; no pay-to-play found
